newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia to seek extradition of 2,400 suspects.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia to seek extradition of 2,400 suspects.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Monday it would seek the extradition of up to 2,400 former officials of a Marxist military junta accused of genocide and crimes against humanity.

Chief Special Prosecutor Girma Wakjira said 2,481 people out of 5,198 charged with genocide and crimes against humanity during the 17-year rule of the Marxist military junta were known to have left Ethiopia or were hiding inside the country.
He said extradition requests were delayed so evidence was properly compiled and their whereabouts were established.
He said his office would publish summonses against those whose involvement in crimes was proved beyond doubt. If they failed to appear in court, extradition requests would be issued.

"If countries which gave sanctuary to persons suspected of involvement in genocide and human right crimes want to try them under their own legal system, Ethiopia will provide not only documentary evidence but is ready to pay all expenses and send witnesses," Girma said.
Only 46 of 71 former Marxist officials accused of genocide and violations of human rights have appeared on trial so far.
The remaining 25 of the 71, including Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam who ruled from 1977 until his overthrow in 1991 and now lives in exile in Zimbabwe, are being tried in absentia.
Their trial was adjourned last week until October 7.
